Illegal immigration is such an odd topic in the news. Too much time is spent arguing the veracity of these people. Most of them probably are just hardworking, poor people looking for a better life.... but that isn't the point:

To me, it seems real simple.

  1. People are breaking the law, we need to enable law enforcement to enforce laws, without using racial profiling. For instance, it is illegal for a cop to pull up in Lowe's parking lot at 9AM on a wednesday and ask to see driver's licenses.
  2. Our borders need better protection to enforce the law. We need to increase the priority of border protection spending.
  3. We need to crack down on companies and people hiring undocumented workers. Department of Labor - start doing your jobs!
  4. We need to remove the tax incentives to companies building across the border - which is acting like a stepping stone for illegal immigration.

I also think it is really simple to do all the above, while still offering a greater number of work visas to immigrants who pass background checks, and have a good work history.

If you ask me doing number 3 will make number 2 unnecessary. Illegals come here for jobs, make it so that only those who are citizens, residents, or those who have a work visa are allowed to have a job. Once you do that you'll find that there won't be a lot of people coming here.

They will put the one guy, who is legal, on the books and not inquire about the rest of them. Then the one guy will get paid via a check if the construction company is smart, or cash if they aren't, that one guy will pay the rest in cash.

Number 3 is the basis for why 1 and 2 are issues. Add that the companies in question lobby to keep the status quo and thus protect their profits. Cheap labor is the basis of the immigration problem. As long as companies are able to hire people for cheap, all of the other problems will be unsolved.
